title: Cislunar transfer, delta-v, Hydrolox and cryogenic closure audit for OTA-TEC-0082
question: Source-grounded audit of the exact OTA-TEC-0082 CYGNUS CTV dossier. Using primary, peer-reviewed and official sources, assess only the externally checkable engineering layer: (1) distinguish the dossier's simplified 'Hohmann transfer' wording from realistic patched-conic / multi-body Earth-Moon transfers and check representative delta-v and 72-84 h transfer-time assumptions for LEO to lunar-orbit / cislunar destinations; (2) close the Tsiolkovsky arithmetic for the inherited fictional mass set 85 t dry, 180 t maximum loaded mass, 75 t LH2/LOX and claimed 5.2 km/s delta-v at representative hydrolox vacuum Isp, explicitly reporting which combinations are physically incompatible without changing the fictional canon; (3) verify real RL-25 and RL10 thrust/Isp characteristics and assess whether the dossier's inherited '4 x RL-25, 450 kN, 465 s' can be treated only as a fictional type label/analogy rather than an exact real engine specification; (4) assess cryogenic LH2/LOX storage and boil-off management over multi-day cislunar missions, including passive versus active thermal-management constraints; (5) check whether the stated standard-flight split around 3.1 km/s TLI + 0.8 km/s LOI and any inferred reserve are technically defensible for the stated route, and separate LLO, EML-2/Gateway and other destination requirements; and (6) identify wording that should be narrowed, reclassified or left explicitly [F/OFFEN]. Do NOT validate or alter fictional introduction dates, fleet counts, operator names, ticketing/economics, NOXIA costs, unlocks, production values, journey timings used only for gameplay, or any other balancing value.
why_now: OTA PR #14 deliberately introduced OTA-TEC-0082 as the next OTA->NOXIA technical-object pilot and explicitly deferred a source-pinned cislunar delta-v / engine / cryogenic closure audit until after merge. The production inventory now reports OTA-TEC-0082 as uncovered, so this is the intended first backlog intake rather than an automatically generated rerun.
real_world_anchor: Tsiolkovsky rocket equation; NASA and peer-reviewed cislunar trajectory/delta-v references; official RL-25/RL10 performance data; cryogenic fluid management and hydrogen/oxygen boil-off engineering for multi-day spaceflight.
novelty_reason: First exact-source-revision engineering closure audit for the canonical CYGNUS CTV. Existing OTA technical-object research covers Starport Launcher, Pelican, RL-25 and Gateway but not the CYGNUS vehicle-level mass/delta-v/transfer/cryogenic closure.
